exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
subtopic: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples
question: Who are Australia’s first inhabitants?
options: European migrants after World War II
The Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples
explanation: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples were here long before European settlement. They have the oldest continuous cultures and traditions in the world.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: Australia’s first inhabitants are the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
subtopic: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples
question: Where are Torres Strait Islander people from?
options: Islands off the coast of Western Australia
Islands between the northern tip of Queensland and Papua New Guinea
Tasmania and the islands of the Bass Strait
The deserts of the Northern Territory
explanation: Aboriginal people are from mainland Australia and Tasmania. Torres Strait Islander people are from the islands to the north of Queensland.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: Torres Strait Islander people are from islands between the northern tip of Queensland and Papua New Guinea.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: On what date did the First Fleet arrive from Great Britain?
explanation: European settlement began when the First Fleet arrived on 26 January 1788. That date is now marked each year as Australia Day.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: arrived from Great Britain on 26 January 1788

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: How many ships made up the First Fleet?
explanation: The booklet describes the First Fleet as the first 11 convict ships sent from Great Britain. They arrived on 26 January 1788.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: the first 11 convict ships

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: Who was the first Governor of the colony of New South Wales?
explanation: Captain Arthur Phillip was the first Governor of New South Wales. The colony survived and grew as more convicts and free settlers arrived.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: The first Governor of the colony of New South Wales was Captain Arthur Phillip.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: In what year did the gold rush begin in New South Wales and Victoria?
explanation: Gold was discovered in 1851 and people came from all around the world. In ten years Australia’s population more than doubled.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: In 1851, a ‘gold rush’ began

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: Who were the first large group of migrants to Australia who were not from Europe?
options: Americans who came after World War II
Indian people who came after Federation
Chinese people who came during the gold rush
explanation: The gold rush drew people from all over the world. Chinese people arriving then were the first large group of migrants not from Europe.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: Chinese people arriving at this time were the first large group of migrants not from Europe.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: In what year were the separate colonies united into the Commonwealth of Australia?
explanation: In 1901 the colonies became a federation of states. The national parliament, government and High Court were set up under the new Constitution.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: In 1901, the separate colonies were united into a federation of states called the Commonwealth of Australia.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: After which event were Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples included in official estimates of the population?
options: The end of World War II
explanation: In 1901 the population count of about four million left out Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples. That changed only after a Referendum in 1967.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: it was not until after a Referendum in 1967 that they were included in official estimates

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: What is Australia’s national language?
explanation: English is the national language and part of the national identity. Other languages are valued too, including more than 100 Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: Australia’s national language is English.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: How many states and mainland territories does Australia have?
options: Five states and three mainland territories
Seven states and one mainland territory
Six states and two mainland territories
explanation: The Commonwealth of Australia is a federation of six states and two mainland territories. Each has its own capital city.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: There are six states and two mainland territories.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: What is the capital city of Australia?
explanation: Canberra is the national capital, in the Australian Capital Territory. Sydney is the largest city, but it is the capital of New South Wales.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: Canberra is Australia’s capital city

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: Which is the largest state in Australia?
explanation: Western Australia is the largest state, and Queensland the second largest. Perth is the capital of Western Australia.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: Western Australia is the largest state.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: Which is the smallest state in Australia?
explanation: Tasmania is the smallest state and is separated from the mainland by the Bass Strait. Victoria is the smallest of the mainland states.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: Tasmania is the smallest state, separated from the mainland by the Bass Strait.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: Which was the first colony established by the British?
explanation: New South Wales was the first British colony. Its capital, Sydney, is the nation’s largest city.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: New South Wales was the first colony established by the British.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: The Great Barrier Reef runs along the eastern coast of which state?
explanation: Queensland is the second largest state and its capital is Brisbane. The Torres Strait Islands lie to its north and the Great Barrier Reef runs along its eastern coast.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: the world-famous Great Barrier Reef runs along its eastern coast

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: Uluru is an icon of which part of Australia?
explanation: The Northern Territory has a tropical north and dry red desert in the south. Its icons include Uluru, Kata Tjuta and Kings Canyon.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: Northern Territory icons include Uluru, Kata Tjuta and Kings Canyon.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: Anyone can deliver an Acknowledgement of Country.
explanation: A Welcome to Country is performed by an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander custodian of the local region. An Acknowledgement of Country can be given by anyone, usually the chair of a meeting.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: Anyone can deliver an Acknowledgement of Country.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: On what date is Australia Day celebrated each year?
explanation: Australia Day is a public holiday in every state and territory. It is the anniversary of the arrival of the First Fleet in 1788.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: On 26 January each year, we celebrate Australia Day.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: On what date is Anzac Day commemorated each year?
explanation: Anzac Day is a solemn day of remembrance. It honours all Australians who served and died in wars, conflicts and peacekeeping operations.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: Anzac Day is commemorated on 25 April each year.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: Anzac Day is named after the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps. Where did it land on 25 April 1915?
explanation: During World War I the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps landed at Gallipoli in Türkiye. Anzac Day is held on the anniversary of that landing.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: which landed at Gallipoli in Türkiye during World War I on 25 April 1915

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: How many points does the Commonwealth Star on the Australian National Flag have?
explanation: The Commonwealth Star sits under the Union Jack on the flag. Six of its points stand for the six states and one for the territories.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: This star has seven points

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: On the Australian Aboriginal Flag, what does the yellow circle represent?
explanation: The Aboriginal Flag is black, red and yellow. Black represents the Aboriginal peoples, red the earth, and the yellow circle the sun.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: The yellow circle represents the sun.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: Which two animals support the shield on the Commonwealth Coat of Arms?
explanation: The Coat of Arms is the official symbol of the Commonwealth of Australia. A kangaroo and an emu, both native animals, stand on each side of the shield.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: A kangaroo and an emu support the shield on each side.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: What is Australia’s national flower?
explanation: The golden wattle is a small tree that grows mainly in south-eastern Australia. Its green and gold are also the national colours.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: Australia’s national flower is the golden wattle.

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: What are Australia’s national colours?
explanation: Green and gold are the colours of the golden wattle. The uniforms of national sports teams are usually in these colours.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: Australia’s national colours are green and gold

exam_version: Our Common Bond testable section (test from 15 November 2020)
question: What is the name of Australia’s national anthem?
explanation: The anthem is sung on occasions of national importance. These include citizenship ceremonies and major sporting events.

source.title: Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond (testable section)
source.quote_under_25_words: ‘Advance Australia Fair’ is Australia’s national anthem.
